requirements.invariant: The browser must record editor content only after explicit informed consent.
The server must bind every accepted edit to one authenticated session and contiguous revision; exact retries must be idempotent.
An independent verifier must reconstruct all accepted Unicode edits and reject changed, omitted, reordered, or wrongly bound evidence.
Assessment expiry and source/event/session resource limits must be enforced by the server and derived from policy.json.
Unknown, malformed, unsupported, missing-model, and uncertified inputs must not be converted into an authorship accusation.
Paste behavior, typing style, and client-reported event trust must not independently determine authorship or cause automatic penalties.
Dataset evaluation must exclude session, author, task, repository, exact-source and normalized-token overlap between splits and hold out generator families.
A frozen threshold must be selected without calibration/test labels; low-FPR qualification must use an independent human-session confidence bound.
Synthetic examples and deterministic passing tests must never establish real-human or any-provider detection efficacy.
Only the session token holder may export/delete active records; errors must not echo submitted source or credentials.
A real browser must exercise consent, editing, server persistence, submission, export/readback, and deletion.
All native skill execution and missing external evidence must be reported truthfully; the full release gate must fail closed.
Candidate code must never execute in the assessment server; model loading must avoid pickle and verify configured model identity.
Provider-agnostic detection quality must be measured on independently sourced, consented real-human sessions and unseen model families at predeclared session-level FPRs.

non_claims: No real-human accuracy is established by synthetic examples.
Native release-chain evidence is required, not fabricated.
